newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian analysts recommend stock picking for Q2 97.
newsitem.headline: Belgian analysts recommend stock picking for Q2 97.

text.p: Amid uncertainty about Wall Street's future direction and with bond market rates seen in a range, Belgian stock market analysts are recommending individual stock picking in the second quarter of 1997.
"In the context of stable long term yields fluctuating around present levels we don't expect a further strong improvement in the Bel-20 index," said Thierry Masset at Vermeulen Raemdonck/BBL.
He forecast the Bel-20 leading share index - now around 2,079 points - would range between 2,050 and 2,200 points.
"We see unchanged levels in the coming weeks, unless there are dramatic statistics in the United States," he added.
Positive surprises in the recent wave of company results should provide some underlying support in the weeks ahead, analysts said.
Stefan Casteleyn at Corluy and Co said his previous Bel-20 forecast for 2,300 points at the end of 1997 still stood.

Out of favour for Vermeulen's Masset were interest rate sensitive stocks, though he was positive on Belgo-French banking group Dexia CC. Insurer Fortis AG was still a good long term growth story, though he considered it a "hold".
Some industrials and cyclicals were also being recommended by brokers, including oils group Petrofina and cement company CBR.
Steel maker Cockerill Sambre was considered a somewhat speculative "market outperformer" by Bank Degroof, and a "buy" by Vermeulen-Raemdonck/BBL.
"It's time to be positive on Cockerill - it will benefit from price rises for steel and in hot dipped galvanised products," Masset added.
Corluy's Casteleyn said he favoured holdings, which were at a large discount to net asset value.
On the other hand some of the previously considered growth stocks, including financials like Fortis, had gone up fast already and so were looking the most dangerous, he said.
Analysts were mixed on retailers, generally preferring Delhaize over rival GIB for its visibility and long-term earnings prospects.
Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) profiles producer Deceuninck was also liked for its U.S. prospects following recent acquisitions.
Casteleyn said shares still looked relatively cheap when estimated dividend yields were compared to 10-year Belgian bond yields.

Technically, weekly stock market graphs and indicators were showing no sell signals - unlike those for Wall Street - said KB-Securities analyst Francis Smolders. However he was negative on a daily basis.
The Bel-20 index rose sharply during the first quarter, rising to peak at 2,220 points in early March from 1,895 at the end of 1996.
